title: Sukkot and the simple joy of eating outside in the fall
dek: Sukkot runs through October 2 this year, and its tradition of meals in outdoor booths is a lovely way to meet the season.
body: This week many Jewish families are celebrating Sukkot, which began at sundown on Friday, September 25, and ends at nightfall on Friday, October 2. It is also called the Feast of Tabernacles or the Feast of Booths.

The holiday marks the autumn harvest and remembers the Israelites' forty years of wandering in the desert after leaving Egypt. One of its best-known traditions is eating meals in a sukkah, a temporary booth built outdoors, often decorated with branches, fruit and handmade art.

I do not want to speak for anyone else's tradition, and the people who keep it can explain it far better than I can. What I find beautiful from where I sit is the idea of stepping outside to share a meal and paying attention to the season as it changes.
Many of us spend fall moving indoors. A holiday that invites people back out into the open air, together, feels like a good reminder for everyone.
If you have friends or neighbors celebrating this week, wish them a happy Sukkot, and if they invite you into their sukkah, say yes.
